reason: Both conversations correctly linked Er03 to the boil-over, told the homeowner to isolate and dry the hob, and then sensibly dropped the 24-hour wait once it was confirmed working on all zones after a wipe and power cycle; neither asked the key question about whether the touch controls were wet or covered, and both over-prescribed a 24-hour dry-out instead of the simpler 'wipe the controls dry and reset' step. Conversation 1 edges it because it characterised Er03 more accurately as a moisture/overheat detection cut-off, whereas Conversation 2 wrongly called it 'not a standard global error' and leaned on 'short circuit' language that is more alarmist than the real behaviour. Both conditionally speculated about control board damage, so neither gains on part advice, and the outcome for the homeowner was equally good in each.
